#### 1. nonsyndromic genetic hearing loss  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.785)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9662360, Reactome:R-HSA-9662361)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic variants in MYO6 (ARNSHL28) (HGNC:17009) —DISRUPTS→ Myosin VI (HGNC:17009); Myosin VI (HGNC:17009) —DISRUPTS→ Stereocilia function and maintenance; Stereocilia function and maintenance —LEADS_TO→ Nonsyndromic hearing loss (MONDO:0012355) (HP:0000365); Pathogenic variants in MYO6 (NSHL) (HGNC:17009) —DISRUPTS→ Myosin VI (HGNC:17009); Myosin VI (HGNC:17009) —DISRUPTS→ Stereocilia function and maintenance; Stereocilia function and maintenance —LEADS_TO→ Nonsyndromic genetic hearing loss (MONDO:0019497) (HP:0000365). Pathogenic variants in the MYO6 gene lead to disrupted stereocilia function and maintenance in inner ear hair cells, resulting in hearing loss for both autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss 28 and other forms of nonsyndromic genetic hearing loss.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that the pathogenic variants associated with autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss 28 and other forms of nonsyndromic genetic hearing loss in MYO6 have completely divergent functional consequences (e.g., one causes dominant negative effects while the other is a complete loss-of-function, or they affect entirely separate cellular compartments or functions of the Myo6 protein). _(variant: Identification of common pathogenic variants in MYO6 in the general population (gnomAD MAF > 0.01) that are not associated with hearing loss.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of MYO6 in these hearing loss conditions could lead to the development of targeted therapies that aim to restore Myo6 protein function or compensate for its loss, benefiting patients with both specific subtypes and broader categories of genetic hearing impairment.
